title: Magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor
source_used: Quantum Computing Report (Google Quantum AI study in Science)
key_facts: Google Quantum AI published the study in Science
First physical hardware implementation of magic state cultivation, on the Willow superconducting processor
T-states with record 99.99(1)% logical fidelity (error rate at or below 0.0001)
Older distillation was projected to use 90-95% of a quantum computer's physical qubits
Method: noisy state injected into a distance-3 color code, error-filtered, then switched into a distance-5 surface code
Team invented a self-referential benchmarking protocol to bound fidelity
quote_evidence: In a milestone study published in Science, experimentalists and software engineers at Google Quantum AI have demonstrated the first physical hardware implementation of magic state cultivation, achieving a 40-fold error reduction and producing T-states with a record 99.99(1)% logical fidelity.
The hardware achievement directly validates Google's foundational 2024 cultivation theory framework.
why_it_matters_hint: Making T-states cheaply removes one of the biggest qubit costs of fault-tolerant quantum computing.
